The uniformity of evidence-based treatments in practice is a complex issue. While evidence-based practice (EBP) has been shown to improve patient outcomes and lead to more efficient performance, the individual therapist and various factors such as treatment supervision and financial burden can influence the effectiveness of these treatments. 

In some cases, such as tuberculosis treatment in China, poor treatment supervision and heavy financial burdens can lead to non-adherence to standard treatments. Additionally, simply providing surgeons with current evidence may not be enough to change their practice. 

However, studies have also shown that certain interventions, such as allocating resources to effective methods for improving adherence to follow-up and using reminders, can improve patient outcomes. Furthermore, residency training sites can provide patient care opportunities similar to those found in community practice, which can help promote uniformity in evidence-based treatments.

Overall, while there is no uniformity in the application of evidence-based treatments, it is clear that individual factors, treatment supervision, and financial support all play a role in the effectiveness of these treatments. More needs to be done to enhance treatment supervision policies, financial supports, and education to promote the uniform application of evidence-based treatments in practice.
